text:
When you look at me, Clori, I imagine

myself a horizon filled with light before your eyes;

your sun acts on the dark affection

as it acts on the serene spirit;


and when from within my breast I try

to return high reflections to the effective light,

what is luminous and pure responds well,

but the earthly exhales its mists.


Then your gaze is not sun, but dawn,

it dispels its imperfect vapor;

but if perhaps it strives to form a cloud,


against itself it shines;

because the moment it rises to your sphere

your noble radiance inflames and gilds it.

translation.title: When You Look at Me, Clori, Full of Light
translation.editorial_note: The translation keeps the sun/dawn metaphor for a beloved gaze that transforms earthly mist.
